title: Bound outbound torrent URL and provider fetches and propagate cancellation
description:
Review: Astra adversarial review — performance.

## Source locations

- `server/api.go:81`
- `server/api.go:123-133`
- `server/search.go:62-69`

## Evidence

addTorrentFromURL uses http.Get via DefaultClient, with no overall timeout and no incoming request context. The 10 MiB limit bounds bytes only, not time. fetchSearchConfig also uses http.Get and unbounded io.ReadAll; a stalled body prevents its background refresh loop from continuing.

## Reproduction / validation

A remote server can send headers then stall its body indefinitely; POST /api/url remains pending even if its browser disconnects, since the request context was not passed. Use a local httptest origin to reproduce without adding a torrent. Remote provider-config fetch is likewise unbounded in time and size.

## Impact

Dead providers leave UI operations permanently busy and retain HTTP connections/goroutines after the requester is gone; provider-config refresh can get stuck or allocate an unbounded response.

## Acceptance criteria

Use a configured HTTP client with finite dial/header/body or total timeout, pass API request context through URL fetch, and bound provider-config body size with an explicit oversize error. A stalled local origin must time out; client cancellation must stop upstream reads promptly.

## Confidence

high

## Completion evidence

Torrent and provider-config fetches share a finite 15-second total-timeout client, validate HTTP status, and read at most limit+1 bytes for explicit oversize errors. Torrent URL fetches receive the incoming request context; provider config is capped at 1 MiB and torrents at 10 MiB.

Full server race suite, embedded Go build, type and whitespace checks pass. Stalled local origins time out; cancelling the API request promptly cancels the upstream read. Tests exercise both provider-config timeout/oversize, torrent timeout/cancellation, generic oversize and non-2xx status.

Live browser: aborting POST /api/url after 300 ms closed the actual stalled upstream connection at 0.299 s. An un-aborted request returned 400 with an actionable body-read timeout at 15003 ms; origin observed closure at 15.0 s. Then submitted public Big Buck Bunny through the Omni URL control; its metadata loaded and retained download appeared at 100%. Removed test torrent and stopped the stalled-origin server, preserving completed public media.
